why: "The next strictly smaller value to the right" is the textbook monotonic-stack query. Scanning from the right, keep a stack of candidate prices that increases from bottom to top; pop anything >= the current price, and the top that remains is its answer.
hints: A brute-force scan to the right for each ticket is O(n^2). When can a later price never be anyone's answer again?
If price p sits at i, any price to its right that is >= p is useless for every ticket left of i: p is closer and at least as cheap. So discard those, leaving an increasing stack.
Iterate i from n-1 down to 0: pop while stack top >= prices[i], answer is stack top or -1, push prices[i]. Each price is pushed and popped once, O(n).
pitfalls: Strictly smaller: equal prices are not an answer, so pop on >=.
Return the price itself, not its index.
